notes: dc CALL 2026-10-21: Tesla Q3 2026 earnings call, a Q&A-format webcast (results deck released about 3:00 pm CT, webcast 4:30 pm CT); speakers Musk (CEO), Taneja (CFO), Elluswamy (AI), Moravy (vehicle engineering), Axelrod (IR). Transcript from Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT TSLA 2026Q3 (one AV call, saved verbatim in gather/raw_documents/av_earnings_call_transcript_TSLA_2026Q3.json); the deck (pf_rel_20261021_1) and the 10-Q (pf_10q_20261022) were read from the prefetched text. The results of 2026-10-21 are citable from 2026-10-23 and the 10-Q from 2026-10-24, so both can back drivers at as_of 2026-10-27.

dc FRESHNESS: the latest results are Q3 2026 (deck and 8-K 2026-10-21, 10-Q 2026-10-22). Reported to the 10-Q date: revenue 28,046M flat year over year, gross profit 5,494M (19.6% margin), operating income 718M (2.6%), net income to common 787M, EPS 0.22 diluted (non-GAAP 0.48), operating cash flow 6,263M, capex 4,732M, free cash flow 1,531M, cash and short-term investments 45,447M.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO Taneja, call): FY2026 capex guidance revised to 'approximately $20 billion' (from 'in excess of $25 billion' in the 10-Qs of 2026-04-23 and 2026-07-23) 'as a result of managing our capital deployment efficiently', funded primarily from operating cash flow. The 10-Q of 2026-10-22 says 'in excess of $20 billion'. Nine-month capex is 13,014M, so the guide implies about 7.0bn in Q4 2026. Capex 'for the next few years would continue to expand' (Robotaxi fleet, Optimus capacity, solar, self-driving compute, a semiconductor fab); Musk: capex 'a little lower than we anticipated', 'more meaningful next year and then noticeable, in the tens of billions, in 2028'. This is management's statement, not a forecast of this engine.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, 10-Q Liquidity): in September 2026 Tesla signed three unsecured credit agreements with aggregate commitments of $30 billion (a $20bn delayed-draw term loan maturing 2029-09 whose undrawn commitment steps down to $10bn at 12 months, $5bn at 15 months and zero at 18 months; $8bn 5-year and $2bn 364-day revolvers replacing the $5bn RCF). 'We don't plan to make any draws under any of the new facilities in this calendar year.' The 10-Q also says heightened capex 'will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow' and that the business 'may include additional funding': external funding is a stated possibility, not a plan with an amount.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, call): operating expenses 'as previously guided' keep rising sequentially (R&D 2,761M versus 2,371M in Q2 and 1,630M a year ago: SI and self-driving costs including compute depreciation, chip development, preproduction costs for Optimus, Megapack 3 and Semi; SBC from the 2025 CEO award); 'This trend of growing OpEx would continue until we commercialize these new products.' No numeric opex guide.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (Musk and CFO, call): demand 'is exceeding our production by a significant margin'; the highest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years; deliveries constrained primarily by production, and the deck names battery availability as the limiting factor on the vehicle production ramp; days of supply 11. FSD is 'the biggest driver for demand'; over 75% of North American deliveries signed up for a paid FSD subscription at delivery (each delivery carries a free month); 1.74M active FSD subscriptions. Musk expects EU-wide FSD approval 'maybe within a few months... surprised if it takes longer than Q1' (2027); nine EU countries approved so far. Opinion and management expectation, not evidence of outcome.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (CFO, call): automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits rose from 16.3% to 18.1% sequentially, 'driven by a higher mix of deliveries in APAC'; commodity price increases and interest rate changes are headwinds partly offset by changes to the vehicle financing programs; Model S and X were discontinued in mid-2026 (10-Q). Energy gross margin rose from 20.4% to 33.1%, 'primarily attributed to tariff refunds recognized in the quarter and warranty true-downs resulting from alignment with our vendor on certain cell-related costs to be reimbursed by them' (the warranty amount is not given); Taneja expects ASP improvement and further margin improvement as Megapack production rises. Services and other margin 15.9%, an all-time high. Management says Megapack is 'almost sold out' for 2027, with the highest-ever order rate and backlog, driven by data center demand.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (call): Robotaxi: Cybercab rides began in Austin on 2026-09-03; the Cybercab fleet in Austin grew tenfold in a month; Dallas next month; six cities in the Robotaxi service; 24/7 operation and higher-speed roads targeted by year end; a $0.30 per paid mile unit-economics goal (whether it is a cost or a price per mile is not stated) is not yet reached, with a 'path' to it; customer-owned vehicles joining the fleet around Q2 2027 (v15 software); Cybercab to customers 'by the end of this year' in small numbers (the vast majority of the fleet will be Tesla-owned). Musk: Robotaxi 'will not move the needle this quarter', 'noticeable probably in Q2' 2027 and 'a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year'. These are management hypotheses without revenue disclosure.

dc MGMT 2026-10-21 (call): Optimus: early production on the Fremont line (a 1-million-unit-per-line design) 'at least a year, maybe a little longer' to reach an annualized rate of 20,000 units a week; design still changing (the hand); deliveries to outside companies 'toward the end of next year' (2027); AI5 chip integration around April 2027; 10,000-20,000 bots needed for self-play data; an Austin Optimus factory is under construction. Terafab: the Austin research fab begins commissioning machinery in H1 2027, a first test chip around May or June 2027, useful chips at volume 'around Q3 of 2028' (aspirational); capital 'in the tens of billions' up to early 2028 and 'north of $100 billion' long term, with the Tesla versus SpaceX split not yet decided. Vehicle capacity: 'aiming for 5 million vehicles a year by approximately 2030' (Musk: 'a good shot'); Berlin expansion permits applied for; Semi factory in Nevada started. All are management aspirations.

dc MGMT 2026-10-22 (10-Q Item 5) and call: the board formed a special committee of disinterested directors 'to explore deepening Tesla's relationship with SpaceX, which could be through certain arrangements including without limitation a business combination'; 'no assurance that any Transaction will be consummated' and any deal needs the committee's recommendation and shareholder approval. Management declined to answer questions on a potential SpaceX merger on the call. Tesla also invested $2.0bn in SpaceX common stock in March 2026 (under 1% ownership, fair value 2,865M at 2026-09-30, sale restrictions expire December 2026), sells Megapacks to SpaceX (221M in Q3) and carries 729M of receivables from it (588M billed for undelivered Megapacks). The Terafab capital split between Tesla and SpaceX is also open.

dc SHARES: 3,952,757,946 shares outstanding on 2026-10-15 (cover page) versus 3,751M at 2025-12-31, but Q3 2026 weighted basic shares were 3,240M and diluted 3,541M (301M dilutive awards): restricted stock awards are excluded from EPS shares until earned. Note 9 describes the 2025 CEO Performance Award (423.7M unearned restricted shares, 12 tranches, market-cap milestones from $2.0tn to $8.5tn, each needing operational milestones, with an offset of $334.09 per share at vesting), the 2018 award exercised in Q2 2026 (about 304.0M options exercised, about 17.5M shares net settled, shares issued as restricted shares vesting 2028-01-19) and the forfeiture of 96M shares of the 2025 interim award. The cover-page count is about 412M above the diluted EPS count and the 10-Q does not itemize that gap; the analyst must set point-in-time ownership shares and EPS shares apart and decide the treatment of unvested restricted stock. A Q2 2026 asset acquisition of an SI hardware company was paid with $1.95bn of stock and equity awards ($1.73bn conditioned on service or deployment milestones).

dc ONEOFFS Q3 2026 (quarter case): symmetric adjustments entered in understand/quarter_case.json: gains = IEEPA tariff refunds in cost of revenues 786M, bitcoin mark-to-market 288M; charges = tariff refunds owed to energy customers 339M (revenue), regulatory-credit reversal 475M (revenue), SpaceX mark-to-market 142M, certain tax items 44M after tax. Net effect on normalized net income about -48M (787M reported to 739M normalized). Not sized and therefore not adjusted: the energy warranty true-downs and the cell-vendor reimbursement the CFO cites, foreign-currency losses on intercompany balances (302M in Q3, recurring in nature), the 275M expense of the 2025 CEO award (non-cash, recurring). The Q3 effective tax rate of 16% is depressed by mix and the non-deductible CEO award expense.

dc FORECAST HINTS (facts, not forecasts): Q4 2026 capex implied by the guide about 7.0bn versus 4.7bn in Q3 and 5.8bn in Q2; regulatory credit revenue 417M, 542M, 380M, 146M, 113M over the last five quarters (Q3 net of a 475M reversal) while the RPO of that program is 384M; Energy revenue fell 16% year over year to 2,881M (customer tariff refunds, lower Megapack ASP, fewer Powerwall deployments) although deployments rose to 13.7 GWh; Services and other revenue +33% year over year; operating leases (new vehicle count) fell from 167,163 to 133,720 in a year; accrued warranty rose 26% to 10,138M in a year; energy storage RPO from contracts over a year is 10.73bn, of which 4.80bn within 12 months.

dc SEGMENTS: Tesla has two reportable segments (automotive, which includes services and other and regulatory credits, and energy generation and storage). The 10-Q and 10-K give segment revenue, cost of revenues and GROSS PROFIT (the CODM's measure) but no segment operating income, so segment operating_income is null in the segments list and the gross profits are entered as facts (dc_seg_gp_*). Revenue lines (automotive sales, regulatory credits, leasing, services and other) are entered for five quarters from the deck.

dc CUSTOMERS: no customer is reported at 10% or more of revenue (consumer-driven business); the 10-Q says one customer exceeded 10% of accounts receivable at 2026-09-30 (current; not named; at Dec 31 2025 none did). SpaceX receivables of 729M are about 16% of the 4,636M receivables, so SpaceX may be that customer, but the 10-Q does not say so.

dc RISK 1 (10-K Item 1A, Risks Related to Our Ability to Grow Our Business): 'We may experience issues or delays in developing, launching and ramping the production of our products, services and features, or we may be unable to control our manufacturing costs' (Cybercab, Semi, Optimus, Megapack 3, cells); the Q3 deck lists battery availability as the current limit on vehicle volume. [pf_10k_20260129]

dc RISK 2 (10-K Item 1A): supplier and cell dependence: 'Our suppliers may fail to deliver components according to schedules, prices, quality and volumes' (single-source suppliers) and 'We will need to maintain and significantly grow our access to battery cells' (relies on Panasonic and CATL; own 4680, LFP, cathode and lithium refining are in early ramp). [pf_10k_20260129]

dc RISK 3 (10-K Item 1A): demand, competition and the cycle: 'Our future growth and success are dependent upon demand for our electric vehicles and adoption of autonomous driving solutions' and 'We face strong competition for our products and services' (automotive is cyclical; interest rates, incentives and tariffs affect demand); automotive sales revenue was down 9% in 2025 and the company-wide revenue was flat in Q3 2026. [pf_10k_20260129; 10-Q Item 2]

dc RISK 4 (10-K Item 1A): key-person and governance: 'We are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk' (who also leads SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink and The Boring Company), pledged-share and forced-sale risk, and the 2025 CEO Performance Award's possible misdirection of focus; a possible SpaceX combination is being explored by a board special committee (10-Q Item 5). [pf_10k_20260129; pf_10q_20261022]

dc RISK 5 (10-K Item 1A): capital intensity and funding: the business 'is capital-intensive... We may need or want to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity, equity-related or debt securities'; capex above $20bn in 2026, Terafab in 'tens of billions', and undrawn facilities of $30bn that step down. [pf_10k_20260129; pf_10q_20261022]

dc RISK 6 (10-K Item 1A and Note 13; 10-Q Note 11): autonomy product liability, defects and regulation: 'Our business may suffer if our products or features contain defects' and 'We may be required to defend or insure against product liability claims'; Benavides verdict (129M compensatory plus 200M punitive; appeal pending at the 11th Circuit, immaterial accrual), FSD and Autopilot class actions and a securities class action (Western District of Texas, motion to dismiss pending), NHTSA, SEC and DOJ information requests; Robotaxi expansion depends on regulatory approvals. [pf_10k_20260129; pf_10q_20261022]

dc RISK 7 (10-K Item 1A, international operations; MD&A): trade policy, incentives and regulatory credits: tariffs and retaliation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and the shrinking regulatory credit programs (credits revenue 417M to 113M year over year), export and sourcing exposure to China (revenue by country is gather_macro's lane); the Supreme Court IEEPA ruling produced one-time refunds in Q3 2026. [pf_10k_20260129; pf_10q_20261022]

dc RISK 8 (10-K Item 1A, financing programs and warranty; Bots): 'We may be unable to effectively grow, or manage the compliance, residual value, financing and credit risks related to, our various financing programs' (resale value guarantee exposure of 4.42bn, up from 3.45bn) and warranty reserves that 'may be insufficient' (accrued 10.1bn); the Bots (Optimus) program has 'yet to commercialize' and 'there is no guarantee this business will be successful'. [pf_10k_20260129; pf_10q_20261022]

dc SBC: Q3 2026 stock-based compensation was 1,165M (2025: 663M), of which 275M is the 2025 CEO Performance Award (only the 20-million-vehicle milestone is probable; unrecognized 9.74bn over 8.9 years; the not-probable milestones carry 105.82bn to 120.37bn if they become probable) and 124M other performance grants (580M probable and 3.22bn not probable remain unrecognized). SBC excluded from non-GAAP; the engine keeps it as a recurring cost.

dc SOURCES: no CFO commentary exhibit exists separately; the Q3 deck (exhibit 99.1) is the release. Documents read from the prefetched text: reading/release_2026-10-21__exhibit9914.txt, 10q_2026-10-22.txt (notes 1, 3, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14 and MD&A), 10q_2026-07-23.txt and 10q_2026-04-23.txt (capex guidance and Q2 segments), 10k_full.txt (RPO, concentration, segments, supply and Item 1A headings), release_2026-07-22 and release_2026-04-22 and release_2026-01-28 (outlook sections: qualitative only).
gaps: Tesla gives no numeric guidance for revenue, deliveries, production, margins, opex, tax rate or share count in the deck, the 10-Qs or the call; the only numeric guides are FY2026 capex (about or above $20bn, cut from above $25bn), 400 MW of SI training compute by year end and no draws on the new credit lines in 2026. The earlier outlook sections (2026-01-28, 04-22, 07-22) are qualitative. The guidance track record therefore rests on capex only.

Segment operating income is not disclosed (gross profit is the CODM measure); there is no split of R&D and SG&A between automotive, energy, Robotaxi, Optimus and SI compute, so the profitability of the new businesses cannot be separated from the core.

Vehicle ASP, cost per vehicle, FSD revenue or ARR, FSD churn and Robotaxi revenue and unit economics are not disclosed (management says FSD metrics will be shared 'as it scales'; an analyst's ARR estimate near $1bn drew the reply 'I think the numbers you shared are correct' from the CFO on the call, an unaudited remark).
The warranty true-down and cell-vendor reimbursement that lifted Q3 energy gross margin are not sized; the tariff refunds are sized (786M in cost of revenues, 339M in revenue).

The 412M gap between the 3,953M cover-page shares and the 3,541M diluted EPS shares is not itemized in the 10-Q (unearned 2025 award shares of 423.7M and the restricted shares from the 2018 award exercise are the candidates named in Note 9).

No purchase-commitment or supply-contract table was found in the prefetched 10-K or 10-Q text (battery cell, semiconductor contract manufacturing from July 2025 and Terafab equipment orders are described only in words); Tesla's energy RPO (10.73bn) and regulatory-credit RPO (384M) are disclosed, vehicle backlog is described but not quantified.

Only one transcript was available (the Q3 2026 call, Q&A format without a prepared outlook slide); the Q4 2025, Q1 and Q2 2026 calls were not read, so earlier management statements are known only from the 10-Qs and decks.

Quarter case and econ case: the economics registry has no vehicles x ASP or energy storage model, so the econ review is 'unclassified' (not forced); vehicle, storage and Robotaxi KPIs are carried in this fragment instead.
stopped: Stopped reading the other three earnings decks, the DEF 14A and the 10-K supply notes in full once capex guidance, the Q3 deck, the 10-Q notes, risk factor headings and the call were covered; no IR-site or EDGAR refetch was needed because the prefetch saved every document.
